description: An attacker sets up a rogue Wi-Fi hotspot named 'CoffeeShop_Free_WiFi' near a popular cafe. When users connect, the attacker intercepts their traffic and performs SSL stripping by intercepting HTTPS requests and downgrading them to HTTP. Login forms on popular websites appear normal but transmit credentials in plaintext.
indicators: User accesses website with HTTP instead of HTTPS despite expecting secure connection; Browser security indicators (padlock) are missing or show warning; Unusual network gateway or DNS responses redirecting HTTPS traffic to HTTP; Login credentials captured in plaintext by attacker

description: A home router is infected with malware that intercepts outgoing traffic. The malware actively strips HTTPS connections to banking websites down to HTTP, allowing attackers to capture sensitive authentication tokens and passwords during login.
indicators: Bank website loads without HTTPS and browser warns about insecure connection; Users report sudden unexpected logouts or account breaches; Network traffic analysis shows downgrade of HTTPS requests to HTTP; Presence of unusual certificates or absence of expected SSL certificates

scenario: Malicious browser extension facilitating SSL stripping
description: A malicious browser extension is installed on users' machines through social engineering. The extension intercepts web requests and strips SSL from secure websites, redirecting users to HTTP versions where their login credentials are logged and sent to the attacker.
indicators: Users notice missing HTTPS padlock on frequently visited secure sites; Browser extension with excessive permissions installed without user awareness; Unexpected redirects from HTTPS to HTTP during authentication flows; Captured credentials transmitted to external IP addresses via extension
